sections.title: Look Back (Review)
paragraphs: The Bible teaches that many generations after Abraham, the Israelites became slaves in Egypt. In their slavery, the people cried out to God for deliverance. God heard their cry and sent a man named Moses to deliver them. God told Moses to lead His people to the Promised Land. Moses preformed many miraculous signs to prove that God had spoken to him. Finally, after many signs, the Egyptians let the Hebrew people go.

sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: God led His people out of Egypt, and He gave His law to the people. These laws also included the 10 Commandments. God wanted His people to be holy and to fellowship with him. He did not want them to be like the other nations.
Let’s read some verses from the Holy Scriptures, the Bible, that relate to this story.

These verses teach us that God first redeemed Israel and then gave them His Law, teaching them how to live in freedom with Him. These commandments show our weakness — all people sin by breaking God’s Law. We can never become righteous on our own. But here is the good news! The Law is not the end; it points to Jesus Christ. Because Jesus never sinned, our sins can be forgiven through Him. His teaching shows us the Law’s deepest meaning — to love God and to love one another. God's grace comes first, the Law shows us our need, and Jesus fulfills it all.
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little — how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Ask Jesus to help you keep God’s law. Start today by doing something to show love to your family. How can you show your family God’s love today?
I hope you enjoyed this story. When can we meet again?
Do you think someone else should hear this story?
